remedies.name: The Knee-High Barrier Hugelkultur Bed
remedies.target_scenario: Disturbed soil with stains, industrial rubble, or heavy metals risk
materials_needed: Salvaged stones, concrete chunks, or red bricks for retaining walls
Wet cardboard (3 layers thick), heavy woven burlap, or canvas tarps
Forearm-thick rotting tree branches or old logs (decaying wood)
Armfuls of dry fallen leaves, straw, or dead brown grass
Bucketfuls of fresh green weed tops (roots removed) or clean garden trimmings
Bucketfuls of clean dark forest soil or settled compost
Cold campfire wood ash and crushed charcoal

step_by_step_instructions.name: Perimeter Demarcation & Debris Clearing
step_by_step_instructions.action: Mark a bed 1 pace wide (arm's reach from both sides) and 3 to 4 paces long. Clear surface metal scrap, glass, and loose rubble by hand to bare ground.

step_by_step_instructions.name: Toxin Isolation Barrier
step_by_step_instructions.action: Lay down 3 overlapping layers of wet cardboard, burlap, or heavy canvas directly over the stained/rubble ground. Ensure zero gaps so underlying contaminants and persistent weeds cannot migrate upward.

step_by_step_instructions.name: Wall Construction
step_by_step_instructions.action: Stack salvaged stones, whole bricks, or logs around the perimeter until the wall reaches knee-high (~45 to 50 cm high).

step_by_step_instructions.name: The Sponge Core (Hugelkultur)
step_by_step_instructions.action: Fill the bottom half of the bed (shin-deep) with forearm-thick rotting logs and branches. This spongy dead wood absorbs seasonal rainwater and slowly feeds crops for years.

step_by_step_instructions.name: The Nitrogen Booster Layer
step_by_step_instructions.action: Pack in two armfuls of green weed clippings and 1 handful of crushed charcoal/ash per pace over the wood core.

step_by_step_instructions.name: The Root Cap (Growing Soil)
step_by_step_instructions.action: Top off the remaining hand's depth of the bed with an even blend: 2 bucketfuls of rich forest topsoil/leaf-mold + 1 bucketful of dark decomposed compost per pace of bed length. Lightly water and let settle for 3 suns.

remedies.safety_guarantee: Completely isolates crops from contaminated ground below. Deep knee-high depth ensures safe root zones for heavy feeders and surface-fruiting crops.

remedies.name: Deep Salvage Container & Barrel Growing System
remedies.target_scenario: Severe chemical contamination, toxic fuel spills, or zero available clean ground
materials_needed: Empty metal food drums, halved plastic barrels, sturdy wooden crates, or stacked salvaged tires
Hammer and metal spike to punch bottom drainage holes
A handful of gravel or coarse broken brick fragments for bottom drainage
Clean topsoil, leaf-mold, and charred wood fragments

step_by_step_instructions.name: Container Preparation & Drainage
step_by_step_instructions.action: Punch 4 to 6 thumb-thick drainage holes in the bottom perimeter of the container to prevent anaerobic standing water.

step_by_step_instructions.name: Base Gravel Filter
step_by_step_instructions.action: Fill the bottom two finger-widths with coarse gravel or clean crushed brick fragments so drainage holes do not clog with silt.

step_by_step_instructions.name: Clean Soil Blending
step_by_step_instructions.action: Fill to two finger-widths below the rim with a mixture of: 3 bucketfuls clean soil + 1 bucketful rotted leaf mold + 2 double-handfuls of crushed campfire charcoal (biochar).

step_by_step_instructions.name: Watering & Settling
step_by_step_instructions.action: Soak with clean rainwater until water drips steadily from the base holes. Allow 1 full sun cycle before sowing.

remedies.safety_guarantee: Zero root contact with contaminated terrain. 100% controlled clean substrate for root crops like potatoes and carrots.

remedies.name: The No-Dig Lasagna Sheet Mulch Bed
remedies.target_scenario: Compacted urban hardpan or dry depleted clay with minimal stones
materials_needed: Thick cardboard or 5 layers of scrap paper/newspaper
Green layer materials: fresh grass trimmings, clover, young thistles/nettles
Brown layer materials: dry shredded leaves, straw, dry brush twigs
Bucketfuls of rich compost and wood ash

step_by_step_instructions.name: Cardboard Smother Base
step_by_step_instructions.action: Water hard ground thoroughly. Lay thick cardboard directly over existing weeds. This smothers weed roots and attracts earthworms to drill through hardpan.

step_by_step_instructions.name: Alternating Green & Brown Layers
step_by_step_instructions.action: Add a hand-depth of brown dry leaves, then a hand-depth of green plant trimmings. Repeat 2 times until the pile reaches mid-thigh height (it will settle to knee-high).

step_by_step_instructions.name: Top Planting Pockets
step_by_step_instructions.action: Spread 1 bucketful of clean compost per pace on the surface. Cut small slits through the mulch to plant sturdy seedlings directly.

remedies.safety_guarantee: Creates 100% new topsoil above compacted ground without backbreaking digging or destroying fragile soil biology.
